clue.text: Scotsman looking for position in the Ridings?

parts.note: Jock is the stock nickname for a Scotsman
eyeing, spelt here without its middle E, means looking at something

explanation.surface: A Scot is peering about, trying to find a spot somewhere in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ridings are the old divisions of Yorkshire, but the question mark points to riding horses: jockeys manoeuvre for position in a race, the idiom 'jockeying for position'.
explanation.definitionFit: Manoeuvring for advantage in a horse race is what riders do, giving the idiom for scrambling for position.

clue.text: James the candlestick-maker ?

parts.note: the outlaw James's first name is also an old word for a branched church candlestick, made like the tree of David's father

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery-rhyme 'candlestick-maker' is a tease: the candlestick itself carries the name of the American outlaw, and the clue fuses the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A large branched church candlestick bears this name, which was also the first name of the outlaw James.

clue.text: Netted — or went over the — top ?

definitions.meaning: netted means made as clear profit after deductions
went over the top, as a hurdler or high jumper gets over the bar without touching it

explanation.walkthrough: The dashes split 'over the top', suggesting excess, so that the second reading is simply jumping over something.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing money is taking it as net profit, and clearing a bar is jumping over it.

clue.text: Have company consider the idea

definitions.meaning: to give a notion some thought

explanation.surface: A suggestion that someone should invite people round.
explanation.definitionFit: To host guests is one sense; to hold a thought in mind, as with a suggestion, is the other.

clue.text: Build any bit out of this, that's for sure

indicators.note: the letters are made out of the words given, rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A challenge to construct something from odds and ends, with confidence it can be done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' signals that the letters of BUILD ANY BIT are rearranged; 'this' links the instruction to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Without doubt is the sense of the adverb, a phrase used to say something is certain.

clue.text: A snare for blue ribbon types

definitions.text: A snare for blue ribbon types

parts.words: A snare for blue ribbon types
parts.note: a trap for catching game, and also a spirit that tempts teetotallers, who once wore a blue ribbon to show they had taken the pledge

explanation.walkthrough: The Blue Ribbon movement was a temperance campaign whose members wore a blue ribbon; 'blue ribbon' here does not mean a prizewinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a hunting trap and also a strong spirit, a temptation to abstainers.

clue.text: Six of them to die

parts.note: a gaming die is a cube, so it has six sides with spots on

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests six people condemned, but 'die' is the singular of dice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cube has six flat surfaces, and on a gaming die each one shows a number of spots.

clue.text: Cassius blamed no stars for such poor service

definitions.text: Cassius blamed no stars for such poor service

parts.words: Cassius blamed no stars for such poor service
parts.note: in Julius Caesar Cassius says the failing lies not in our stars but in ourselves; a bad serve at tennis has the same name

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is 'The fault, dear Brutus, is not in our stars, but in ourselves'; 'service' then switches to tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Cassius locates blame in people rather than stars, and a tennis serve that lands wrong is called by the same word.

clue.text: Nuclear part not well set up by atomic writer

parts.note: the core is the central part, the nucleus, of something

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word for not well is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A piece of a nuclear reactor is badly installed by a scientist who writes about atoms.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Corelli was a popular Victorian novelist whose books include The Mighty Atom, hence 'atomic writer'; 'set up' turns ILL into LLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Corelli wrote the novel The Mighty Atom, so she is a novelist with an atomic title.

clue.text: Shakespeare as a key writer (Wordsworth)

parts.note: Wordsworth's poem Scorn not the Sonnet says that with this key Shakespeare unlocked his heart, so the playwright is a writer of fourteen-line poems

explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth wrote that with the sonnet as 'key' Shakespeare 'unlocked his heart', so 'key writer' is not a musical key or an important author.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of fourteen-line poems, which Shakespeare was, as Wordsworth's poem about that form says.

clue.text: How the paper is "put to bed"?

definitions.text: How the paper is "put to bed"?

parts.words: How the paper is "put to bed"?
parts.note: a newspaper is put to bed when it goes to press; a bed is made up with linen, and paper comes in single pieces

explanation.walkthrough: Printers say a newspaper is 'put to bed' when it is finished and sent to press; the clue takes that literally, as if the paper were dressed with bed linen.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper supplied in single flat pieces is in this form, and a bed made up with linen is too.

clue.text: What's one turn anyway? Small matter, no charge

indicators.note: read as any way, in any order you like, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a single turn as trivial and free of cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' reads as 'any way', telling you to rearrange ONE TURN; 'What's' just links. The definition is physics: a tiny particle of matter with no electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle in the atomic nucleus with no electric charge, a minute piece of matter.

clue.text: Pope's human attribute

parts.note: Alexander Pope wrote that to err is human, to forgive divine

explanation.walkthrough: Pope is the poet Alexander Pope, not a pontiff: 'To err is human, to forgive divine' comes from his Essay on Criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope's line says making mistakes is what humans do, so a mistake is the human quality he names.

clue.text: Beauty packs a gun, so what's her game ?

indicators.note: a beauty packing a gun carries it inside, so the word for beauty goes round the rest

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
gat is old American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: A glamorous woman is armed, and someone asks what she is up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's her game' invites a guess at her scheme, but the game is literal: a table game in which balls are knocked into holes on a board. GAT is American gangster slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A table game in which balls are struck into numbered holes or cups on a board.

clue.text: Tucks into Edam in gross fashion

definitions.text: Tucks into Edam in gross fashion

parts.words: Tucks into Edam in gross fashion
parts.note: eats cheese greedily, piggishly devouring it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucks into' is British for eating heartily; 'in gross fashion' tells you the eating is greedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat gluttonously, wolfing food down in a greedy way.

clue.text: People are furious when they see it

definitions.text: People are furious when they see it

parts.words: People are furious when they see it
parts.note: the idiom to see a certain colour means to become very angry

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is the idiom 'to see red', to become very angry, read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'see' plus this colour means to fly into a rage, like a bull at a cape.

clue.text: Those in the home team in tears

indicators.note: the team is placed in the tears, so the word for tears goes round it

parts.note: rents are rips or tears in cloth
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Members of a home side who are crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' looks like weeping but means rips, and 'home team' tempts you to read a football side; 'Those in the home' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who live in a house or place are its inhabitants.

clue.text: Another way to fill in the tea interval

indicators.note: the letters are filled in a new way, made to fit another pattern, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion for another way to spend the break for a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fill in' asks you to rearrange the letters of TEA INTERVAL; 'the' is a link. The definition is the noun sense, another option.
explanation.definitionFit: An option available instead of another, a different route or choice.

clue.text: Perseus stands by her in heaven too

definitions.text: Perseus stands by her in heaven too

parts.words: Perseus stands by her in heaven too
parts.note: in myth the hero rescued the chained princess, and their constellations are neighbours in the sky

explanation.walkthrough: 'stands by her' is both loyalty and position: Perseus saved her from the sea monster, and the two constellations lie side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ethiopian princess rescued by Perseus, who is also a constellation next to his in the night sky.

clue.text: Divers means, say, of getting a rise

definitions.text: Divers means, say, of getting a rise

parts.words: Divers means, say, of getting a rise
parts.note: a flexible board used by swimmers to bounce up before plunging, also a start for advancement

explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like the old word for various ('divers means'), but it is people who dive.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexible board from which swimmers jump, and figuratively a starting point for rising in life.

clue.text: Neat thief

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so a cattle thief

explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle thief, neat being an old term for oxen and cows.

clue.text: This used to be read through

definitions.text: This used to be read through

parts.words: This used to be read through
parts.note: a Latin preposition still used in English, which readers render as through or by

explanation.walkthrough: The clue says this short Latin word was read as 'through'; 'read through' looks like perusing something.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin preposition meaning by means of or through, as in miles per hour.

clue.text: Peter put on hat used for roofing work

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: Peter Pan, J M Barrie's boy who never grew up
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Someone called Peter puts on a hat to go and work on the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places PAN above TILE in this down entry. A curved roof tile is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved S-shaped clay tile laid on roofs.

clue.text: Showed how Pluto performed

parts.note: Dis is another name for Pluto, Roman god of the underworld
played means performed, as music or a role

explanation.surface: Someone describes how a dog or a god put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluto is not Disney's dog or the planet but the god of the underworld, also called Dis; 'how' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to exhibit it or put it on view.

clue.text: The French welcome holidays

parts.note: le is French for the
ave is a Latin greeting, hail or welcome

explanation.surface: French people are glad to have time off.
explanation.walkthrough: AVE is the Latin greeting 'hail', used in crosswords for welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Time off work, as in annual leave, is a period of holiday.

clue.text: Has he more than nine points, or about three ?

definitions.text: Has he more than nine points

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word or goes round the three letters

parts.note: taken as written
three points of the compass, west, north and east, following the earlier mention of points

explanation.surface: A question about a scorer who has passed nine points, or perhaps reached about three.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'possession is nine points of the law' means the possessor has the advantage. 'about' puts three compass points, W, N and E, inside OR.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessor of property, who by the proverb has nine-tenths of the law on his side.

clue.text: But not how Labour describes the Tories

definitions.text: But not how Labour describes the Tories

parts.words: But not how Labour describes the Tories
parts.note: the Tories are the political wing on one side, but their opponents would never say they were correct

explanation.walkthrough: Labour and the Tories (Conservatives) are Britain's main parties; the Tories are on the political right, though Labour would not call them correct.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the conservative side of politics and also correct, which Labour would deny of its rivals.

clue.text: Invalid has trouble following the ravines

parts.note: null means invalid, as in null and void

indicators.note: has gets into trouble, so its letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A sick person struggles after the gullies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' looks like a sick person but means void; 'following the' is a link. Nullahs are dry riverbeds or gullies in India.
explanation.definitionFit: In India, a dry riverbed or gully is called by this Hindi-derived word.

clue.text: Order to dog when it's disorderly

annotationWithheld.why: Order to dog when it's disorderly (3): the clue parses cleanly to SIT (order to dog; an anagram of IT'S), but the held answer is SOT, whose middle letter is unchecked and which no reading of the clue produces
annotationWithheld.clue: Order to dog when it's disorderly

clue.text: Looking for what a cat may do ?

definitions.meaning: the proverb says a cat may look at a monarch, so it can view a ruler

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'a cat may look at a king' means anyone may look at the great; read as two words, the answer is what the cat does.
explanation.definitionFit: Searching is the first sense; the proverb 'a cat may look at a king' gives the split see plus a monarch.

clue.text: A red worsted ?

parts.note: a Russian man's name, so a red, and also a hard-wearing twilled woollen fabric

explanation.walkthrough: 'A red' suggests a Communist, here a Russian with this first name; 'worsted' is a woollen cloth, not 'beaten'.
explanation.definitionFit: A durable twilled wool fabric, and a Russian forename, hence a Communist or red.

clue.text: Witness meant otherwise in the trial

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged in another way, so the letters of meant are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone giving evidence in court meant something different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' asks for the letters of MEANT in a new order, placed after the word for trial; 'in the' is a link. Testament as witness means bearing testimony to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence or proof of something, as in a tribute that stands as testimony to a person.
